Specific books ( brick-and-mortar dollar or dime boxes are still the cheapest if you don't care to find a particular title), protein powder, firearm accessories , computer components , car components , electronics, everything is still cheaper online in absolute price - and when you factor in the colossal time savings...

About half of my clothing purchases fit into that category; the other half I either don't care or I've bought that brand before and know what size is correct.

There is one thing that is more expensive online (but always has been): perishable food. I did an experiment and compared the numbers between months of shopping in person and months of ordering groceries online, and it ends up costing me in the long run the same amount to pay the extra for delivery versus going retrieving it myself, so now except in cases where I need something right now… I take the time savings and order delivery groceries.

50% of my attempted eBay purchases have ended poorly or just been straight up scams. Maybe I'm just bad at eBay, but it's not worth the hassle to me and I don't use it anymore except to estimate prices for things are not in current production or in stores.

Finally, one thing that brick-and-mortar cannot compete with is the breath of selection that online stores offer. If I need a specific electronic component, there are anywhere from 2 to 50 different specific styles or brands available for me to choose from, often with many different user reviews of each. It will never be cost-effective for a brick-and-mortar store to offer that. RadioShack is an excellent example : they used to be the go to source for electronic components for makers, but many of them don't even have an electronic components shelf anymore, and I've literally watched it shrink from an entire section of the store down to one drawer at all my local RadioShacks. I don't even bother going there anymore, because I know their entire catalog by heart because it is so small and they never have what I need anymore. I will pull up at most four websites, and have dozens of options with customer reviews to choose from for my components now. Regrettably, I will have to wait for them to ship it be delivered...
